# Tutorial: Hub notification plugin

Build a Hub runtime plugin that receives HAPI notification events and logs them.

## What you will build

A Hub runtime plugin that registers a notification channel. When HAPI emits ready, permission, task, or session completion events, your plugin receives a narrow `PluginNotificationEvent` DTO and logs it.

## 1. Create files

```bash
mkdir -p tutorial-notification-logger/dist
cd tutorial-notification-logger
```

Create `hapi.plugin.json`:

```json
{
    "id": "com.example.tutorial.notification-logger",
    "name": "Tutorial Notification Logger",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "pluginApiVersion": "0.1",
    "description": "A tutorial Hub plugin that logs HAPI notification events.",
    "runtimes": {
        "hub": {
            "entry": "dist/hub.js"
        }
    },
    "contributions": {
        "hub": {
            "notificationChannels": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-logger",
                    "displayName": "Tutorial Logger"
                }
            ]
        },
        "web": {
            "settingsPanels": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-notification-logger",
                    "title": "Tutorial Notification Logger",
                    "description": "Configure the prefix used by the tutorial notification logger.",
                    "components": [
                        {
                            "kind": "text",
                            "text": "This Hub runtime plugin logs notification events."
                        },
                        {
                            "kind": "schemaForm",
                            "title": "Logger options",
                            "fields": [
                                {
                                    "key": "prefix",
                                    "label": "Log prefix",
                                    "type": "text",
                                    "defaultValue": "[tutorial-plugin]"
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    },
    "permissions": {
        "network": ["https://example.com/*"],
        "secrets": ["TUTORIAL_WEBHOOK_TOKEN"]
    }
}
```

Create `dist/hub.js`:

```js
export function activate(ctx) {
    const prefix = String(ctx.config.get('prefix') ?? '[tutorial-plugin]')
    const token = ctx.secrets.get('TUTORIAL_WEBHOOK_TOKEN')

    ctx.logger.info('Tutorial notification logger activated. tokenPresent=%s', Boolean(token))

    ctx.notifications.registerChannel({
        async send(event) {
            ctx.logger.info(
                `${prefix} type=${event.type} session=${event.session.id} agent=${event.session.agent ?? 'unknown'}`
            )
        },

        async dispose() {
            ctx.logger.info('Tutorial notification logger disposed.')
        }
    })
}
```

## 2. Install and enable on the Hub target

```bash
cd ..
hapi plugins install-local ./tutorial-notification-logger --target hub --enable --reload
```

If Hub is not running, omit `--reload`; the plugin will load next time Hub starts.

## 3. Set optional config

```bash
hapi plugins config set com.example.tutorial.notification-logger prefix "[notify]" --target hub --reload
```

Config is saved to `$HAPI_HOME/plugins.json`. Do not put secrets there.

## 4. Provide declared secrets
The manifest declares `TUTORIAL_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`. Export it in the environment that starts Hub:

```bash
export TUTORIAL_WEBHOOK_TOKEN=dev-token
hapi hub
```

A missing declared secret creates diagnostics but does not expose the secret value.

## 5. Inspect and debug

```bash
hapi plugins list --target hub
hapi plugins inspect com.example.tutorial.notification-logger --target hub
hapi plugins doctor com.example.tutorial.notification-logger
```

Useful failure codes include invalid manifest, missing entry path, disabled plugin, missing secret, and activation failure.

## 6. Iterate

```bash
# edit dist/hub.js or hapi.plugin.json
hapi plugins reload com.example.tutorial.notification-logger
```

Reload disposes HAPI-mediated resources such as registered notification channels. Your plugin must clean up its own timers, sockets, and handles in `dispose()`.
